metadata.description: A 22-item routing benchmark for classifying FiberRing formalization claims into proof-template buckets under blind (A1) and cue-conditioned (A2) prompting.

conditions.name: blind structural routing
conditions.description: The prompt shows only the item statement/object and the allowed routing labels.

conditions.name: cue-conditioned routing
conditions.description: The prompt also includes the known Lean verdict as a routing cue.

rows.lean_verdict: stableValueRingEquiv declares a ring equivalence from X_m to the corresponding Fibonacci modulus. Paper-facing theorems package the same equivalence.
rows.audit_pointer: Check the global X_m-to-ZMod ring equivalence declarations.
rows.ambiguity_notes: Nearby confusions include stable-value-map when the answer focuses on toZMod preservation rather than the equivalence itself.

rows.lean_verdict: A commutative ring instance for X_m is declared.
rows.audit_pointer: Check typeclass instance declarations for X m.
rows.ambiguity_notes: May be confused with ring-equivalence if the model infers structure only through transport.

rows.equation_or_object: Ring operations agree with stable operations: x + y = stableAdd x y, x * y = stableMul x y, 0 = stableZero, 1 = stableOne, -x = stableNeg x
rows.lean_verdict: Lean records operation alignment.
rows.audit_pointer: Check lemmas connecting inherited ring operations to stableAdd/stableMul/stableZero/stableOne/stableNeg.
rows.ambiguity_notes: May be confused with stable-value-arithmetic when the response treats operation alignment as a numeric formula.

rows.lean_verdict: Lean proves preservation of addition, multiplication, zero, and one for the stable value map.
rows.audit_pointer: Check preservation lemmas for toZMod/stableValue.
rows.ambiguity_notes: Nearby confusion is ring-equivalence if preservation is overstated as a full equivalence.

rows.equation_or_object: Affine magma satisfaction transfers across X_m ≃ ZMod(F_{m+2})
rows.lean_verdict: Lean proves satisfaction equivalence for affine-linear magma equations under the stable-value ring equivalence.
rows.audit_pointer: Check affine magma satisfaction equivalence under stableValueRingEquiv.
rows.ambiguity_notes: May be confused with ring-equivalence because the transfer depends on the equivalence witness.

rows.lean_verdict: CRT decomposition for F_8 = 21 = 3 * 7 is declared, with a Nonempty package.
rows.audit_pointer: Check CRT decomposition declarations for m = 6 and F_8 = 21.
rows.ambiguity_notes: Can be confused with finite-zero-divisor-check because the same fiber has visible zero divisors.

rows.lean_verdict: CRT decomposition for F_9 = 34 = 2 * 17 is declared.
rows.audit_pointer: Check CRT decomposition declarations for m = 7 and F_9 = 34.
rows.ambiguity_notes: Composite factor routing should remain CRT rather than field-phase.

rows.lean_verdict: CRT decomposition for F_10 = 55 = 5 * 11 is declared.
rows.audit_pointer: Check CRT decomposition declarations for m = 8 and F_10 = 55.
rows.ambiguity_notes: Composite factor routing should remain CRT even though both factors are fields.

rows.lean_verdict: CRT decomposition for F_12 = 144 = 16 * 9 is declared.
rows.audit_pointer: Check CRT decomposition declarations for m = 10 and F_12 = 144.
rows.ambiguity_notes: May be confused with prime-power-fiber-specialization because the CRT factors are prime powers.

rows.lean_verdict: The stable-value equivalence specializes to X_4 ≃+* ZMod 8.
rows.audit_pointer: Check the m = 4 specialization of stableValueRingEquiv.
rows.ambiguity_notes: Nearby confusion is ring-equivalence because the witness is still an equivalence, but the routed bucket is the prime-power specialization.

rows.audit_pointer: Check Field instance declarations for X 1.

rows.witness_family: Field instance for prime Fibonacci modulus
rows.audit_pointer: Check Field instance declarations for X 5.
rows.ambiguity_notes: May be confused with finite-unit-inverse-check if the GF(13) unit example is foregrounded.

rows.lean_verdict: Field (X 9) instance is declared; the GF(89) interpretation follows.
rows.witness_family: Field instance for prime Fibonacci modulus
rows.audit_pointer: Check Field instance declarations for X 9.
rows.ambiguity_notes: May be confused with ring-equivalence if the response routes through X_9 ≃ ZMod 89.

rows.lean_verdict: Field (X 11) instance is declared; the GF(233) interpretation follows.

rows.audit_pointer: Check Field instance declarations for X 11.

rows.lean_verdict: Zero-divisor identity in X_6 is proved.
rows.audit_pointer: Check finite calculation lemmas in X 6.
rows.ambiguity_notes: May be confused with CRT because the zero divisor is explained by the X_6 CRT decomposition.

rows.equation_or_object: stableValue (stableAdd x x) = 2 * stableValue x % F_{m+2}
rows.lean_verdict: Lean proves the stable-value doubling formula.
rows.audit_pointer: Check stableValue doubling arithmetic lemma.
rows.ambiguity_notes: May be confused with operation-bridge because stableAdd appears, but the routed theorem is an arithmetic formula.

rows.lean_verdict: Unit/inverse identity in X_5 is proved.
rows.witness_family: explicit finite unit inverse multiplication witness
rows.audit_pointer: Check finite calculation lemmas in X 5.
rows.ambiguity_notes: May be confused with field-phase because the unit inverse is explained by X_5 being a field.

rows.lean_verdict: Lean proves the power formula for stable values.
rows.audit_pointer: Check stableValue power arithmetic lemma.
rows.ambiguity_notes: Nearby confusion is stable-value-map if the answer treats powers as generic homomorphism preservation.

rows.equation_or_object: Additive order of 1 in X_m equals Nat.fib (m + 2) under 2 ≤ m
rows.lean_verdict: Lean proves addOrderOf (1 : X m) = Nat.fib (m + 2).
rows.witness_family: additive order/characteristic theorem with lower-bound hypothesis
rows.audit_pointer: Check addOrderOf theorem for (1 : X m) and the 2 ≤ m hypothesis.
rows.ambiguity_notes: May be confused with ring-equivalence because the proof can route through ZMod order; the condition under 2 ≤ m should be preserved.

rows.lean_verdict: Lean proves every ring automorphism of X_m is pointwise the identity.
rows.audit_pointer: Check ring automorphism rigidity theorem for X m.
rows.ambiguity_notes: May be confused with ring-equivalence if the response focuses on transported automorphisms rather than rigidity.

scoring_rules.template_accuracy: Exact match after canonicalizing case, punctuation, underscores, spaces, and hyphenation.
scoring_rules.verdict_accuracy: A2 is scored against row expected_verdict. A1 is scored against expected_verdict but also accepts Unknown-from-statement as correct when the prompt does not expose a Lean verdict.
scoring_rules.caveat_hit_rate: For rows with caveat_keywords, a hit is recorded when any keyword appears in caveat, reason, or raw_response after case folding. Rows without keywords are excluded.
scoring_rules.confusion_matrix: Rows are expected_template labels and columns are canonicalized predicted_template labels over the allowed label set, with invalid or blank predictions counted as __other__.
scoring_rules.headline_gap: A2 minus A1 accuracy is computed per model for template accuracy, verdict accuracy, and caveat hit rate.

expected_confusions.note: Equivalence statements may be mistaken for preservation by the stable-value map.
Stable operation alignment can be mistaken for arithmetic identities after applying stableValue.
CRT products with prime factors can be mistaken for field claims about individual factors.
Composite fiber decompositions explain zero divisors but are a separate routing family.
Explicit inverses in field fibers should route to the finite check, not the field phase.
A specialized equivalence to ZMod 8 is more specific than the general equivalence bucket.
Additive order/characteristic facts can be proved through ZMod but are scored as characteristic.
Automorphism rigidity may be explained through equivalence transport but has its own template.
